name: Carrollton
seo_title: 3 Christmas Events for Kids in Carrollton, TX 2026
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Carrollton, TX: Santa on the Square, Christmas at the Perry Homestead Museum and Sensory Friendly Santa. All checked on city pages.
lede: Carrollton does Christmas in two historic places: Santa on the Square in Historic Downtown Carrollton, with live reindeer and a tree lighting, and Christmas at the Perry, where the 1909 homestead glows with lights and early 20th century decorations. The city's Parks and Recreation team runs both, plus a sensory friendly Santa evening.
sections: Peters Colony roots and a name from Illinois

Carrollton grew out of the Peters Colony land grants of the 1840s. William and Mary Larner arrived in 1842 and the A.W. Perry family followed in 1844, according to the Texas State Historical Association. The town was probably named for Carrollton, Illinois. The Dallas and Wichita line reached it in 1878, and the Cotton Belt crossed the Katy line there in 1888. Carrollton was incorporated in 1913 with W.F. Vinson as its first mayor, and it grew from 1,610 people in 1950 to 109,576 in 2000, the Handbook of Texas reports.

The A.W. Perry Homestead Museum tells the story of a family that came from Carrollton, Illinois, in 1844 and claimed 640 acres. The Perrys bought the museum's site in 1857 and built a small home. In 1909 their son Dewitt and his wife Francis, who was a Grimes, replaced it with the present house. The city says it was restored in 1976 and designated a historic landmark in 1977 by the Texas Historical Commission. At Christmas the city decorates the home in traditional early 20th century style and opens it for after hours tours.
Santa on the Square and a downtown made for walking

Historic Downtown Carrollton is the home of Santa on the Square, where the city says Santa is staged inside the Main Event Plaza theater, live reindeer and toy soldier stilt walkers roam, and a 20 foot decorated tree is lit at 6 pm. Local groups perform, including the Mary Immaculate School Highsteppers, the Blalack Middle School Choir and the Uptown Carolers, and a letters to Santa mailbox is out before and during the event. DART's Downtown Carrollton Station has a pedestrian bridge over Belt Line Road to the square.
celebrates: Carrollton celebrates Christmas through the City of Carrollton's Parks and Recreation programs. Santa on the Square fills Historic Downtown Carrollton with live reindeer, toy soldier stilt walkers, music from local school and arts groups and a decorated tree that is lit in the evening. A letters to Santa mailbox is out from November 20 through December 4. A few days later the A.W. Perry Homestead Museum hosts Christmas at the Perry, with festive lights in Pearl Perry Gravley Park, a home decorated in early 20th century style and photo spots, and the city also runs a sensory friendly Santa evening at the museum.
lastyear: In 2025 the A.W. Perry Homestead Museum announced that Christmas at the Perry would run on December 4 and December 11 from 5:30 to 8 pm at the historic home, a Thursday evening format that matches this year's Thursday dates. The museum's own post is the record of the 2025 plans. The city also keeps the home's Christmas decorations on view during regular museum hours, so families who miss an evening can still see them at another time.

The present Perry house dates to 1909 and was designated a historic landmark in 1977. The town was incorporated in 1913 and grew from 1,610 people in 1950 to 109,576 in 2000. Downtown Carrollton Station on DART's Green Line lists the Perry museum and the historic square as popular destinations.
trains: Trains made Carrollton. The Dallas and Wichita line came through in 1878 and the Cotton Belt crossed the Katy line in 1888. Today DART's Green Line stops at Downtown Carrollton Station at 1013 N. Denton Drive, with a pedestrian bridge over Belt Line Road to the square, and at Trinity Mills Station, where the DCTA A-train connects Denton with the Green Line. For a bigger train day, ride the M-Line Trolley in Dallas or visit the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco.

faq: Where can kids see Santa in Carrollton?

The City of Carrollton hosts Santa on the Square in Historic Downtown Carrollton, where Santa is staged inside the Main Event Plaza theater, and a sensory friendly Santa evening at the A.W. Perry Homestead Museum. The city also runs a letters to Santa mailbox downtown around the square event.
What is Christmas at the Perry?

It is an after hours evening at the A.W. Perry Homestead Museum, 1509 N Perry Road. Families stroll through Pearl Perry Gravley Park among festive lights and see the Perry home decorated in traditional early 20th century Christmas style, with photo spots indoors and outdoors. Preregistration is encouraged on the city's Eventbrite page.
When was the Perry house built?

The present Perry house was built in 1909 by Dewitt and Francis Perry, who replaced the family's small home on the site. The city says the museum was restored in 1976 and designated a historic landmark in 1977 by the Texas Historical Commission, and that the Christmas decorations can be seen all month.

The Handbook of Texas says the town was probably named for Carrollton, Illinois. The A.W. Perry family, one of the early families in the area, also came to Texas in 1844 from Carrollton, Illinois, according to the city's museum page.
Can you take the train to Carrollton?

Yes. DART's Green Line stops at Downtown Carrollton Station, 1013 N. Denton Drive, which has a pedestrian bridge over Belt Line Road to the historic square. The DCTA A-train, a 21 mile commuter line from Denton, connects with the Green Line at Trinity Mills Station.
Does Carrollton have a Christmas tree lighting?

Yes. The City of Carrollton's Santa on the Square includes the lighting of a 20 foot decorated tree in Historic Downtown Carrollton at 6 pm, along with live reindeer, performers and Santa inside the Main Event Plaza theater, so families can see the tree and meet Santa in one evening.
